key_idea: A hopper reaches exactly the vertices at even walk distance, so one start infects a whole connected component iff it contains an odd cycle (is non-bipartite).
sketch: 2-colour every component with an iterative DFS, counting components c and noting whether any is non-bipartite. Joining the components costs c-1 edges, and the merged graph is non-bipartite iff some component was; otherwise one more edge is needed to create an odd cycle (always possible since N>=3). Answer is c-1 plus 1 if all components are bipartite. O(N+M); use an explicit stack because N is 5e5, and remember isolated vertices count as components.
